extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, economists, policy analysts, and patent scholars using USPTO patent microdata
extracted.subtask_short: assigning NBER categories to patent records
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and data standards for creating USPTO Historical Patent Data Files by assigning NBER sub-categories to patents, published and publicly-available unpublished applications, and constructing monthly and annual time series back to 1840. Includes decisions about sources, concordances, classification-era handling, and patents-in-force estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NBER classification as standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the NBER sub-categories (37 two-digit sub-categories aggregated into six main technology categories) to patents and applications to produce economically relevant technology categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NBER classification, developed by Hall, Jaffe, and Trajtenberg (2001), has been widely adopted by researchers and provides a useful standard. The authors apply the NBER sub-categories to granted patents, published and publicly-available unpublished patent applications, and in-force and expired patents to create the USPTO Historical Patent Data Files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concordance construction between USPC and NBER
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a concordance between current USPC class and NBER sub-category and between class-at-issue (class-at-disposal) and NBER sub-category for each classification era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps (as implemented): (1) Update the USPC classification data of the NBER dataset to December 31, 2014 and generate concordance to NBER; (2) Assign NBER sub-category to all patents; (3) Generate concordance between USPC class-at-issue and NBER sub-category for each classification era; (4) Apply the concordance to assign NBER sub-categories to pending and abandoned applications based on class-at-disposal or current class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative NBER classification algorithm and probability threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Match pending and abandoned applications to granted applications of the same vintage and initial classification and assign the NBER sub-category of the granted patent to the pending or abandoned counterpart using an iterative algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execute three iterations of the algorithm. In the initial iteration, match class-at-disposal or current class to NBER sub-category with a probability of at least 75%. Use progressively finer 'classification era' variables (class-level and subclass-level) in subsequent iterations to classify previously ambiguous relationships if the relationship is exclusive at a 75% probability threshold. Result metrics: of 3.5M non-granted apps (1981-2014), 96.91% assigned to a single NBER sub-category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of classification 'era' variables to handle reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct sequential 'classification era' variables from Classification Orders to identify time periods when specific USPC schemes are in force at aggregate, class, and subclass level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'era' begins the day of an order that modifies the class/subclass and ends the day before the subsequent order affecting that class/subclass. Use orders intermediate files (orders, orders_class, orders_subclass) to apply NBER sub-categories when direct matching is ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary data sources and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine multiple data sources: NBER Patent Citation Data File, internal PTO systems (PALM), published patent documents (PGPubs), PTMT continuity extracts, Classification Orders Index, maintenance fee events, and annual published counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, rely on published sources; where unpublished application data are not available, rely on PALM. Update NBER USPC values to 2014 using available sources. Detailed source fields summarized in Table 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion of records (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'regular' utility patents and corresponding utility patent applications; exclude provisional applications, re-issue applications, design patents, statutory invention registrations, plant patents, defensive publications, and non-serialized applications (e.g., some PCT/RCE handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The datasets focus on regular utility patents and exclude other application types. Published and publicly-available unpublished applications are included when they become public (e.g., referenced by a patent or published application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of unpublished, non-publicly-available applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-level data for non-publicly-available unpublished applications are preserved in confidence and are not included in the historical_masterfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unpublished application is not public unless referenced by a patent or published application. Therefore micro-data for non-public unpublished apps cannot be released and are omitted from the public masterfile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of classification failures and special codes
rubrics_metrics.description: When the algorithm cannot unambiguously classify an application/patent, label it with special codes added (70 = Not classified; 80 = Missing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 notes that sub-categories 70 and 80 were added. Report classification success/failure rates (e.g., 96.91% of non-granted apps assigned; 0.52% ambiguous; 2.58% missing USPC data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly and annual time series construction and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce monthly time series (stocks and flows) for publicly-available applications and grants from January 1981 to December 2014 and annual time series of applications, grants, and patents-in-force by NBER sub-category from 1840 to 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly files include incoming applications, grants, abandonments, pending stocks, and monthly_disposal tracks cohort prosecution outcomes. Annual files extend to 1840 but application-level tech disaggregation only starts in 1981 due to data limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and determination of 'disposal' types
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal outcomes for applications ('disposals') are either issuance as granted patents or abandonment; otherwise an application is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowances and rejections are not terminal disposals until issuance or abandonment. For issuance, the dataset uses the day the patent is published as the disposal/issuance date. Abandonment dates are back-filled to reflect the initial response deadline when failure to respond causes abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of left truncation for pending stock reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Because detailed application data begin in January 1981, left truncation biases early pending counts; therefore report estimated stocks of pending applications beginning 73 months after January 1981 (February 1987).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 3 shows survival curves for 1981-1983 cohorts where only 1% of applications remain pending after 73 months; use this to minimize expected undercounting in monthly files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patents-in-force requires accounting for statutory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurately computing patent expiration and patents-in-force must account for statutory patent term changes over history (1790, 1836, 1861, 1980, 1995), maintenance fees (post-1980), and potential patent term adjustments/extensions (PTA/PTE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules used: assume 14-year term for 1790-1836 patents (no expiration records); 1836 Act allowed seven-year extensions so present upper/lower bounds (14/21) for 1836-1861; 1861 fixed 17 years from issue; maintenance fees applied to patents from applications filed on/after Dec 12, 1980; 1995 law changed terms to 20 years from earliest filing (effective June 8, 1995) and requires continuity data to find earliest filing date; include PTA/PTE where data exist to avoid underestimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of maintenance fee and continuity data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use maintenance fee payment data and internal continuity data to estimate patents-in-force and to determine earliest filing dates for patents filed on/after June 8, 1995. Use internal data to identify PTA/PTE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees (due at ~3.5, 7.5, 11.5 years) determine whether patents issued after Dec 12, 1980 remained in force. Continuity data from PTMT custom extracts identify parent applications and earliest filing dates; PTA/PTE identified from internal records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of terminal disclaimers and post-grant cancellation events
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not adjust patents-in-force calculations for terminal disclaimers nor incorporate administrative post-grant proceedings (re-examination) or judicial invalidity actions because machine-readable data are not consistently available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note terminal disclaimers were historically uncommon but increasing (11.9% in 2012). They do not believe omission significantly compromises counts for now, but acknowledge limitations and that omission of post-grant proceedings may affect patents-in-force accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing or inconsistent application and classification dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Back-fill missing application dates in PALM with PTMT Custom Bibliographic Patent Data Extract DVD where available; be aware the DVD is updated only through 2013 so some recent appl_dt may be missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PALM may be missing appl_dt for some records, use PTMT DVD to fill; note that application numbers are sequential and can sometimes be used to infer information, but technological classification is unavailable without concordance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of variables and codebook standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a codebook that defines variables included in each output file (historical_masterfile, monthly, monthly_disposal, annual), their formats, and inclusion indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 4 lists variables (appl_dt, appl_id, pub_dt, disp_dt, disp_ty, exp_dt/exp_dt_max, pta, prior_dt, nber, uspc[_sub], counts by NBER and totals, months_since_filing, etc.). Specify how dates are encoded (Stata days/months since Jan 1960) and intentional missing values for particular historical periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and contents of intermediate and output data files
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce intermediate data files (orders, orders_class, orders_subclass) documenting classification eras and output files (historical_masterfile, monthly, monthly_disposal, annual) with defined variables and aggregation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: historical_masterfile contains micro-level fields (appl_id, pubno, patent, nber, uspc/current class, pub_dt, disp_dt, disp_ty, pta, exp_dt). monthly_disposal tracks prosecution outcomes by monthly filing cohort until disposal or cutoff. annual aggregates from 1840-2014 provide counts by NBER sub-category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publication/patent face dates versus updated current class
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that patent images and bulk XML reflect classification at date of publication, while full-text/current class databases reflect updated classification; choose appropriate class-at-issue or current class depending on matching strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm exploits scrutiny applied prior to patent publication by matching abandoned applications to granted applications from the same vintage and same initial classification. Note that the PTO applies classification updates to pending applications and PGPubs but not to unpublished abandoned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and interpretation guidelines for dataset users
rubrics_metrics.description: Document limitations, caveats, and appropriate uses: datasets enable research into application disposal, dynamics of filings, pendency, abandonment, patents-in-force, and historical trends but have constraints (left truncation, missing unpublished micro-data, unadjusted terminal disclaimers, omitted post-grant proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors highlight expected research uses (e.g., study of administration of patent system, applicant behavior, patent litigation normalization by patents-in-force) and caution on interpreting allowance rates, pendency, and patents-in-force due to measurement choices and historical data gaps.
